dateLabel: built c. 205–87 BCE (debated); wreck c. 70–60 BCE
title: Who built the Antikythera mechanism, and where
summary: The ancient Greek geared calculator is thought to be the work of Hellenistic scientists, but no maker is known and both its place and date of construction are debated.
why: Its sophistication implies a lost tradition of gearwork that no other surviving object shows.
question: Who made the Antikythera mechanism, where, and when?
evidence: Wreck dated 70–60 BCE; construction estimates include 205, 150–100 and about 87 BCE; calendar is Corinthian-type, with month names matching Epirote calendars.
wouldSettle: A second mechanism, a workshop, or text naming its maker.

theories.name: Made at Rhodes
theories.idea: Rhodes was an astronomy centre and the wreck carried Rhodian-style vases.

theories.name: Corinth or its colonies
theories.idea: Calendar month names point to a Corinthian or colonial origin.

theories.name: Epirus client
theories.idea: A Rhodian prototype was modified for a client in Epirus, matching its month names.
